meta.title: Peoples of Middle-earth — Elves, Dwarves, Men of the West, Rohirrim
meta.description: An encyclopaedic overview of the peoples of Middle-earth in Tolkien's world. Elves, Dwarves, Dúnedain, Rohirrim, Haradrim, Easterlings, orcs, hobbits, ents.

hero.subtitle: An encyclopaedic overview of Tolkien's races with links to game armies.

intro: This page summarises the main peoples and races appearing in The Lord of the Rings. The texts are paraphrased, without direct quotations from Tolkien's books. For each people we give origin, main traits and, where applicable, a link to a game army.

alert.pre: The lore on this page is supporting context. For game rules, registration and roles, see

lang_notice: Descriptions of individual peoples are now translated; some terminology may be refined in future updates.

paragraphs: The eldest of the awakened peoples. They woke in Middle-earth long before Men, by the lake of Cuiviénen. Most accepted the call of the Valar and set out on the Great Journey to the West — from them came the **Eldar**. Those who remained became the **Avari**, the wood- and dark-elves.

In the familiar tale of The Lord of the Rings three great elven realms remain from those of old: **Lothlórien** under the protection of Galadriel and Celeborn, **Rivendell** (Imladris) of Elrond, and **Mirkwood**, where Thranduil rules. Apart from these stand the **Grey Havens**, from which the elves are slowly sailing into the West.

In the Third Age the time of the elves in Middle-earth is drawing to an end. The watching kept around the Three Elven Rings (Vilya, Nenya, Narya) preserves the elven realms, but with the destruction of the One Ring their power fades.

in_game.post: brings together different elven strands. We aim for elegance, lighter armour and roleplay in keeping with the atmosphere of the elder race.

paragraphs: The dwarves came from the work of Aulë — one of the Valar — who in his eagerness made them before Eru himself awoke the elves. Eru in the end accepted his work and laid Aulë's children to sleep until they could come into the world after the elves. The Seven Fathers of the Dwarves awoke in the great mountains of Middle-earth.

The eldest and greatest dwarven realm was **Khazad-dûm** in the Misty Mountains — later known as **Moria**, the Black Pit. After its fall the dwarves settled in the east, especially in **Erebor** beneath the Lonely Mountain.
Dwarves are tough, loyal and stubborn. Masters of craft, mining and defence. Their dealings with the elves tend to be cool, with men practical, with Mordor unceasingly warlike.

in_game.post: relies on layered costume, beards, axes, hammers and shields. They give the impression of a craft culture even in camp.

peoples.h2: Dúnedain — Men of the West (Gondor and Arnor)
paragraphs: The Dúnedain are the descendants of the Edain — the three houses of Men who in the Elder Days joined the side of the Free Peoples. After the fall of Beleriand the Valar gave them the island of **Númenor** in the midst of the Great Sea. After centuries of glory, however, the Númenóreans fell into pride, came under the influence of Sauron and turned against the Valar; the island was at last drowned beneath the sea.

Those who remained loyal (the Faithful) escaped and founded two kingdoms in Middle-earth: northern **Arnor** and southern **Gondor**. Arnor slowly fell under the pressure of the Shadow from Angmar and its descendants now wander as the Rangers of the North. Gondor on the other hand survived — though for long centuries without a king, under the rule of the Stewards.

The capital of Gondor is **Minas Tirith**, beneath the White Mountain Mindolluin. At its head stand the Stewards of the House of Húrin; behind them returns at last the ancient line of kings — Aragorn, heir of Isildur.

in_game.post: builds on a martial tradition — white, blue, silver, the sign of the White Tree and the seven stars. At PP we put the emphasis on heraldry and discipline.

paragraphs: The Rohirrim are descendants of the people of Eorl — a tribe of riders who came down from the north into what was then the Gondorian land of Calenardhon. In return for help in battle Gondor gave them this land; thus arose **Rohan**, the “land of the horse-lords”.

The Rohirrim hold their oath dear (Eorl's oath to come to the aid of Gondor), as well as friendship and horses. Their villages are simple, but their lords dwell in halls of timber — the greatest of them is the golden **Meduseld** at Edoras.

What matters in the Third Age is that the Rohirrim and Gondor remain allies, even when time and Saruman's intrigues sometimes pull them apart. The Battle of Helm's Deep and the Pelennor Fields decide their survival as well as the fate of Gondor.

in_game.post: aims at an early-medieval / Northern aesthetic. Spears, shields, axes, layered tunics in earthy tones.

paragraphs: The Haradrim are not a single nation but a general term for the various cultures that live south of Mordor. Tolkien describes them with traits reminiscent of the warm regions of the real world — deserts, oases, long caravans, massive beasts such as mûmakil.

Many of their tribes were long under Sauron's sway — some out of plain enmity towards the West, others for practical reasons: the border with Gondor was bloody for centuries and the mutual debts ran deep. Yet not every Haradrim is a servant of the Shadow; within Harad there are also tribes that hold themselves apart from Sauron's call.

in_game.text: The Haradrim do not necessarily appear at PP as their own army every year — their costume and cultural layer comes and goes with the storyline. If you are interested in a Haradrim styling, contact the organisers.

peoples.h2: The Umbarians — Black Númenóreans and Corsairs
paragraphs: The great southern haven of **Umbar** was founded by the Númenóreans in the Second Age. When Númenor turned to darkness, many of its lords fled here — and from them came the **Black Númenóreans**, who took up Sauron's lead.

In the Third Age Umbar lies in the hands of the **Corsairs** — raiders and traders carrying a human memory of Númenor. Their fleet threatens the coasts of Gondor; their captains are often descendants of the Black Númenórean line and of old dynasties. At the end of the War of the Ring it is by this very route that Aragorn brings the Army of the Dead to victory at Pelargir.

in_game.pre: In our tradition there stands, among others, the crew of the Corsair ship *Hlubina* — see

paragraphs: East of Mordor lie the wide plains and steppes of **Rhûn**. Their inhabitants in the familiar tale are most often found in the role of Sauron's hosts — many waves of them have crossed Middle-earth under his sway. But their tribes are also varied; in some periods of history they fought even against one another.

Tolkien describes them with traits inspired by steppe cultures — wagons, horses, archery, ritual. Yet not every Easterling is a servant of Mordor; over the long ages several of their tribes have made truce with Gondor.

in_game.post: go for an exotic styling — sabres, bows, striking scarves and layered fabrics.

paragraphs: In Tolkien's vision the orcs are **twisted creatures** — the result of Melkor's work upon the elves in very ancient times. They do not stand on their own; they live in clans and hierarchies according to the will of the stronger master. They cannot bear one another for long; what holds them together is either fear or a common enemy.

In the Third Age they fall roughly into: the **Moria orcs** of the Misty Mountains, the **Mordor hosts** directly under Sauron, and **Saruman's** companies, whom the lord of Isengard raised into the **Uruk-hai** — bigger, stronger orcs who can fight even by day.

in_game.post: — bold makeup / masks, grime, layered fabrics, bones, leather. Safe weaponry, but a markedly “orcish” look.

more_beings.intro: Middle-earth is also peopled by other kinds, who play smaller but important roles in the War of the Ring:

items.name: Hobbits
items.desc: — small folk from the Shire. Almost invisible across long histories, yet decisive in the War of the Ring.

items.name: Ents
items.desc: — ancient guardians of the trees. Awakened by Yavanna, in the War of the Ring they rise against Saruman.

items.name: Trolls
items.desc: — Melkor's twisting. In the Third Age they appear in caves, mountains and the morning mist; the stronger ones (oloh-hai) serve Sauron.

items.name: Spider-spawn of Ungoliant
items.desc: — chiefly Shelob on the road into Mordor; smaller spiders in Mirkwood.

items.name: Dragon-kin
items.desc: — in the Third Age the most famous is Smaug; after his fall the dragons fade away, though not necessarily disappear.
